status: Static UI concepts; archive availability, geography, samples and synthesis are illustrative

screens.prompt: Use case: ui-mockup. Create ONE polished wide 16:10 desktop software screenshot, no physical device, no room, no surrounding presentation board. Product ANIMAL ATLAS is a wildlife-event-driven musical instrument with TWO main pages: ATLAS and SOUND STUDIO. Persistent main navigation, session transport and master level must be clear. This is a visual exploration; footer 'Illustrative archive data · UI concept'. All geography/species/source/date values are illustrative, never claim actual available historical records. No airport, pandemic or corporate metrics; no logos, trademarks or text copied from reference. Preserve scientific honesty: fixed acoustic bird detections are not tracks, satellite fixes are distinct, no fictitious motion between stations. Historical composition is an essential feature: selected species + geographic region + exact local date/time interval with timezone + source availability/coverage + a frozen soundscape. Show missing archive intervals explicitly rather than interpolating events. Professional musician-friendly readable controls, not an illegible wall of tiny data. PAIR E · Field Notes. Build directly on original concept 02 FIELD NOTES: warm cream paper grain, olive letterpress cartography, oxblood highlights, elegant editorial serif headings with crisp sans-serif control labels, fine engraved animal vignettes and printed musical notation. A naturalist's field journal made into sophisticated usable software, not a black dashboard. Flat ink/risograph rendering with very restrained tactile sliders. First page ATLAS, with visible SOUND STUDIO navigation. The ATLAS page has a LIVE / HISTORY submode selector; HISTORY selected. A substantial central map or globe occupies 65–75 percent, with honest fixed detection pings, distinct satellite-fix markers and selected regional outline. LEFT narrow 'HISTORICAL SOUNDSCAPE' selection panel: Species 'Tui', Region 'New Zealand', Date '06 Nov 2024', From '05:00', To '08:00', Timezone 'NZDT', button 'Check available data'. Beneath it a small available-data status 'Partial coverage', source 'Archive import', observation resolution 'As recorded'. RIGHT narrow observation journal/provenance panel with selected event timestamp, station location, event kind and source; small 'Edit animal sound' link into studio. BOTTOM substantial archive coverage timeline: show a three-hour window, coloured segments for available records, visibly hatched gap labelled 'No records', range handles and a playhead. Controls 'Freeze soundscape', 'Play', '60x', and observed-time indication. A separate source connection status must not imply the historical interval is live. Illustrative labels only; no manufactured total counts. For Field Notes, maps and timeline are printed/engraved with the right panel like a journal and score marks below. For the globe directions, make the historical selector and coverage timeline coherent with the reference's globe-focused composition. This page is about exploring live nature and choosing a precise moment from genuine available archive material, not editing synthesizer knobs.
